what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 6 of 6: What replaces the Green-function kernel when records form: the response of the formation law to a source. THE PROGRAM'S OPEN PHYSICS QUESTION after block 35 (PR #8180; setting in blocks 13, 26, 34: PRs #8147, #8170, #8178). The gravity lane takes as input a lattice Green-function kernel 1/E(k), E(k) = 2 sum_j (1 - cos k_j). Block 19 found that kernel only in the static (equilibrium comparator) law. The axiom says records FORM: the sphere formation law in level time, linearized about an aligned plane, is theta_{t+1} = P theta_t + noise with phi(k) = (1 + e^{i k_1} + e^{i k_2})/3, u = |phi|^2, and its covariance is sigma^2 phi^s/(1 - u): a plane Green function times a level-time heat kernel, diffusive and drifting. A probe added the exact identity E(k) = 3(|1 - phi e^{i w}|^2 + 1 - u) in level coordinates. TASK: derive the object a gravity-type node would actually see under the formation reading: the linear RESPONSE of the formation law to a persistent localized source (a site whose record is pinned, or a small bias field h at one site acting at every level). (a) Compute the response function exactly for the linear model: R(k, w) = 1/(1 - phi(k) e^{i w}) and its static limit; (b) find its real-space form at long distance on the level planes and along the level direction (saddle point, with the drift removed by the co-moving frame x -> x - t(1,1)/3), with exact constants; (c) decide whether any channel (the static response, the time-integrated covariance, the response in the co-moving frame, a symmetrized combination over the eight corner orders of block 09) decays like 1/r in three dimensions, and if none does, state precisely what decay law replaces it; (d) check the fluctuation-response relation: is the response proportional to the covariance (it is in equilibrium; level time is not equilibrium)? Verify every closed form against exact finite-L sums. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/formation-response-kernel/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/formation-response-kernel/<name>/check.py"
